questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A city that seems interesting and a pleasant place to live

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would recommend everyone to go study abroad

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: 6/10. Everything was scattered in diffrent Emails, that weren't the best structured always, so you had to create your own "to-do" list out of what you could decipher. It would have been nice just to have been given a very structured, this is what you need to do before theese dates.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office was pretty helpfull

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The Erasmus Club students were amazing!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I changed hounding 2 days after arriving in the dorms, since they were filled with mold...
It was actually pretty easy to find housing on my own, but it was intimidating since it was in another country, where you do not know what the chances are of getting scammed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There is lots of "Erasmus" appartments where you still get a exchange feeling and live with multicultural people

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My orgiginal room i moved into  to was one of the most discusting places i have ever seen. I had a freind down there who got mold poisoning for living there (which seems to be pretty normal) and there is practically no communal space in the dorms.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I honestly do not remember the details, just that it was was easy. Only problem was that some deadlines with the approval of couses didnt add up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could talked to the office about stuff, but mostly you were on your own. It helped that we created a messenger group with the rest of UCPH who were going to Charles so we could exchange experiences doing the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I do not really get stressed easyly

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: That you have a week down there to "test" the first lecture of classes, so rather take to many and try a lot first week, and then cancel the classes you do not like.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quality of the lectures where really high, however the exams where so easy that it seemed a little pointless.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was pretty much the same as in Copenhagen, but you were better supported in charles. In general the quality of the lectures was higher in charles than in copenghagen

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very diffrent. In Copenhagen everything more or less follows the same structure, while in Prague it seems that it was up to the teachers to decide more.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urban Social Geography
Soil Mechanics 2
Forest Geography
Demographic Excursion
Applied Geoinformatics
Analysis, mapping and visualization of urban and regional development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Urban Social Geography (You learn a lot about Prague, but also way to much work compared to ECTS)
Demographic Excursion (I went on a 9-day school road triip in the Balkans, i learned so much)
Analysis, mapping and visualization of urban and regional development (Fun if you like Arc GIS, and a good intro course to it)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had a dentist appointment, but my inssurance paid for that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: How extraemly cheap public transport is for students, 3 month student pass for all of prague is 115 DKK, 1 month is 40 DKK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were lots of sport clubs

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on the intro trip if you can! And start a club yourself

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Czecia is a beutifull country filled with natural parks. But Prague also has so much to offer, that you will never discover everything. Also trainsor busses to Berlin, Vienna, Bratislava etc are quite cheap.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: We got a good introduction by the local students in the Eramus Club

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be out there. Do not be affraid to write people a massage if they wanna do anything today. Everyone is in the same box as you, where they want to make freinds, explore and have fun.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Czechs can be quite closed off

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everything seems to be taken care off in Czechia

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go on the intro tour if you faculty has one
2. Be out there, dont be shy to ask people to do something
3. Take intiative for activites yourself

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are unsure, ask someone

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The freindships i made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Exam season (not too challenging though)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
